question: Does recent underlying attacking and defensive performance improve next-match probability forecasts beyond established team strength?
primary_hypothesis: A small pre-specified block of recent underlying performance measurements contains incremental predictive information beyond the frozen Poisson V1 team-strength baseline.
null_hypothesis: The pre-specified Team State performance block does not improve out-of-sample probability forecasts beyond the baseline on a matched fixture population.

temporal_status.constraint: Results remain experimental until the historical publication-time assumption is explicitly audited or replaced by timestamped evidence.

baseline.rule: Freeze the current baseline before challenger fitting; do not tune it using challenger evaluation results.

challengers.purpose: Replace frozen prior-season strength with regularised time-aware attacking and defensive strength plus low-score dependence correction.
Test incremental information from the pre-specified Team State feature block without unrestricted feature search.

evaluation.design: chronological development and evaluation with identical eligible-fixture populations for paired comparisons
evaluation.market_evaluation: separate prospective phase using timestamped available prices and explicit margin removal; no historical profitability claim from model scores alone
evaluation.multiple_testing_rule: All tried feature blocks, windows, transforms and thresholds must be retained in the experiment record.

promotion_rule: No challenger becomes a trusted FRL forecasting model because it looks plausible or wins one backtest. Promotion requires repeatable out-of-sample improvement, acceptable calibration, stable coverage and a clear temporal/provenance contract.
professional_benchmark_note: Current professional/public systems commonly combine dynamic team strength with richer performance evidence. FRL should compare these ingredients empirically rather than inventing an unvalidated composite form score.
